BWV244.prem: 11 April 1727 (Good Friday), St Thomas Church, Leipzig
BWV244.about: Bach’s largest work: the Passion according to Matthew set for two choirs and two orchestras, framed by the vast opening chorus ‘Kommt, ihr Töchter’ and the closing lament ‘Wir setzen uns mit Tränen nieder’. BWV565.about: Its opening — a flourish, a pause, a plunging run and a crashing diminished chord — is perhaps the most recognisable gesture in organ music. BWV806.about: The first English Suite opens with a gentle, flowing prelude and contains two courantes, the second with two ornamented doubles. Like all six English Suites it opens with a substantial prelude before the traditional sequence of allemande, courante, sarabande, lighter paired dances and gigue.
BWV806.ctx: The English Suites are the earliest of Bach’s three great sets of keyboard suites, probably composed in Weimar and completed around 1720. BWV988.about: The Goldberg Variations are Bach’s largest single keyboard work and one of the great monuments of the instrument. A gentle sarabande-like Aria is followed by thirty variations built not on its melody but on its thirty-two-bar bass and harmonic plan.
